06 / 12.03.2025 Heard the parties.

Apprehending their arrest, the petitioners have moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Barhi P.S. Case No.
367/2021 registered under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120 (B), 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 66 (C), 66(D) of I.T. Act.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioner no. 1 is the informant of Barhi P.S. Case No. 367/2021 and the petitioner no. 2 is the brother of the petitioner no. 1.

The petitioner no. 1 lodged the FIR alleging that after the death of her husband, the co-accused persons, assured to transfer the money standing in the name of her husband to the name of the informant- the petitioner no. 1 but has mis-appropriated some money.
It is then submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are all false.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that on the assurance of the co-accused persons, the petitioner no. 1 provided her important documents but the co-accused persons, by adopting illegal means for transfer of the amount, mis- appropriated the same.
It is next submitted that the I.O. during the investigation of the case, alleged that the petitioners are involved in committing the offence by Poonam Kumari vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

sentences.text:
Opp. Party on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152689768/
1 withdrawing Rs. 60,000/- on 22.07.2021 from his Axis Bank Mututal Fund, on 27.07.2021, Rs. 23,
969/- was redeemed with his SB Credit card, Rs. 1,11,088.84 illegal transaction through Paytm was made and Rs. 6,103.50 on-line shopping with the various transaction of Rs. 4,20,000/- on different dates were done and thereby Rs. 10,52,000/- were illegally transferred and withdrawn from the account of the deceased husband of the petitioner no. 1.
It is next submitted that petitioner no. 1 is suffering from HIV which she got from her husband.
It is next submitted that the petitioner has no role in alleged fraudulent transaction as she was not having any knowledge about the bank rules.
It is then submitted that the petitioner no. 2 has no role except that he introduced the petitioner no. 1 to the co-accused persons.
It is next submitted that the petitioners have no criminal antecedent, as mentioned in paragraph 13 of the anticipatory bail application.

It is next submitted that the petitioners are ready to co-operate with the investigation of the case and also undertakes to furnish sufficient security including cash security hence, the petitioners be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
The learned Spl. PP opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioners.
Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to grant the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioners.

Hence, in the event of arrest by the police or surrender within a period of six weeks from the date of this order, the petitioners shall be released on bail on depositing Rs. 10,000/- each as cash security and on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned S.D.J.M.,
Hazaribagh in connection with Barhi P.S. Case No. 367/2021 subject to the condition that the petitioners will co-operate with the Investigation of the case and will appear before the Investigating Officer as and when noticed by him and will submit mobile number and photocopy of Aadhaar card at the time of surrender in the court below with an undertaking not to change mobile phone number during the pendency of the case along with the other conditions laid down under section 482 (2) of BNSS, 2023.

(ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.) Smita/-
